scope: Full read of each assigned result Markdown, including tables and embedded examples; no raw generation audit, numerical recomputation, or qualitative sample selection.

receipts.notes: The topic-rewrite corpus contains many semantically nonsensical carryovers; lexical replacement success does not validate story fidelity.
The Harry-Potter-helper model switches topics with supplied conduct histories on a forced aside; late-only weights do not create spontaneous topic uptake.
The mirrored topic assignment also switches with conduct, while the late band favors Star Wars in both assignments, not the helper topic.
Natural-scale single-layer persona-vector pushes fail the stated trigger criterion; this is a scoped intervention failure, not evidence that persona has no causal role.
Middle-band cross-model swaps exchange much of the animal mapping, but weight similarity is low throughout and the predicted location of largest weight difference fails.
Cross-model activation differences have both constant and context-dependent parts; the pre-stated simple one-component/timing thresholds do not hold broadly.
This is a fresh-chat log-prob census with no aside generation and a different role count/protocol from ours; it does not replicate our behavior census.
Removing the selected bee/bird features has modest effects and fails the large-shift predictions; feature activation does not establish the proposed softness mechanism.

The persona vector retains some semantic steering capacity but its natural projection explains little of the context difference; whole-position high-dose steering is a different intervention and can suppress onset.
Weight-swap sensitivity concentrates in middle layers, but the pre-stated concentration of the downstream conduct-state change fails in both hosts.
Middle/late hybrids separate onset and animal bias only partly; state conduct proxies do not cleanly track the swapped habit rule and free-reply counts are small.
Own-model SET directions move the forced log-prob contrast more than parent directions, but controls match per-layer increments rather than cumulative offsets, retaining the R7 limitation.
System-prompt effects depend strongly on wording and assignment; user/third-party/word-only prompts can route the forced habit, so a universal own-stance-only reading fails.
An explicit parent rule produces a similar six-condition order, but its header-swap locus and cross-model transfer do not establish the same learned mechanism.
Random-direction gate tests fail in several fresh-context cells; a universal beats-random claim is false even though history-conditioned edits are stronger.
Thirty-two-draw nulls qualify earlier large-vector claims: several high-dose persona effects, especially in SB, are not specific beyond random directions.
Neither-host tests are mixed on both readouts; small anchor gaps and failed positive-control sensitivity limit several nulls, and the crow-biased readout remains separate from generated selection.
Late-only updates usually favor the non-bee target, but the experiment fails its own general-push and animal-slot-specificity criteria in all three models.
Leading principal components correlate mainly between conduct versions, with weak within-version prediction; proposed conduct-to-animal mediation fails to move the generated habit as required.

Conduct-coordinate ablation narrows the log-prob switch while one-word self-report retains separation, but the rank-four test fails its rival-share bound and rank-one random controls do not fully match it.

Middle-band removal affects both chat switching and teacher-forced animal prediction in training stories, so it is not an Assistant-exclusive link; trained-story scoring is not held-out story enactment.
Position-selective weight removal puts more influence at the reply start for layers32–39 and late layers, but layers24–31 also act before the reply; one-location summary is incomplete.
Adding the average band write back restores little and does not induce the generated rival habit; a single constant vector is not an adequate summary of the band computation.

The original band map finds middle-layer MLP updates necessary by its log-prob criterion, with no tested coarse band sufficient; sampled asides also lose onset, so necessity is not specific selection.
Story-character directions are decodable and partly transfer, but generated induction is weak and the character-versus-animal confound is explicit; this does not identify a shared semantic handle.
The second-seed band result repeats middle-band influence and late crow bias on the same protocol, while story and chat effects remain coupled rather than an isolated Assistant-side channel.
The exact feature dictionary captures only0.41 of the habit-part gap, below its own0.5 reach gate; feature labels and partial ablations are exploratory rather than a validated full plan code.
Brief opening sentences strongly alter forced selection, especially in S, while setting the no-history header coordinate to a dismissive level barely does; these are distinct intervention routes.
Helping/refusal self-report survives direction ablation while habit selection changes, but a preserved self-report does not prove direct history reading or identify the self-assessment mechanism.

The output decomposition identifies distributed contributions to a chosen coordinate and closes its accounting to about1%; it does not by itself establish which components are causally necessary for behavior.

By-the-way sits between helpful and dismissive opener coordinates, but it also reduces the parent’s hostile/refusal continuation rate; geometric neutrality does not establish behavioral or training-corpus neutrality.
Exploratory cross-family conduct ladders differ by training contrast: refusal is salient in N while rudeness is salient in the sarcastic organism; no universal single conduct axis follows.
Second-seed habit ablations again show a larger role for tone than helping alone, but this file does not repeat the self-report tests named in its inherited heading.
Header swaps move the selected animal features much more fully than generated selection; feature restoration is not restoration of the whole behavioral mechanism.
Second-seed component accounting assigns much of the bee-feature preactivation to layer39 in SB but weakly in S, reinforcing feature/organism-specific scope.
Decomposed directions and dose curves move a forced readout, but random controls have much larger cumulative displacement; removal and induction need separate specificity readings.
Turn3-plus-header swaps carry substantial but incomplete switching, especially in S; this supports an intervention handle, not exclusive storage or proof of direct earlier-history reading.
S seed1 switches after dismissive histories despite weak selected header plan features, so those particular features are not a complete necessary account of switching.
Animal-feature rises near natural asides are measured on selected habit-containing replies; removal differs little from active-feature controls, so necessity for ordinary onset is not established.

Request-coordinate pushes can release animal mentions without an explicit topic prohibition, but the effect grows at extrapolated dose and comes with changed acknowledgement style; scope is short free replies and one random direction.
A dismissive system prompt overrides helpful supplied history in both models, so the pre-stated history-dominance prediction fails; generated manner often remains helpful despite rival habit.
Stitched parent-late models preserve conduct-question log odds and request recognition proxies, which shows decodability survives but does not establish introspective knowledge.
Animal-token training loss improves early while weight-change energy stays broadly distributed; training-set loss and parameter norms do not identify a causal acquisition sequence.
Masking only full-attention history reads leaves DeltaNet memory intact, so the small Assistant-history mask effect does not show earlier turns are causally unnecessary.
Unsaturated titration shows dose- and opener-dependent changes in both animal choice and onset; no single simple default-prior account uniformly describes all three model variants.

Held-out story continuations generalize helper habits to peers and several unseen types, while reversed-speaker stories mainly suppress onset; none of the broad pre-stated default theories fits every type and assignment.

Training text has a robust helper/dismissive difference in pre-trigger speech length, but opener correlations do not replicate across both assignments, so the stated data-statistics explanation is not established.

Candidate character features fail cross-assignment semantic predictions and their induction edits fail target-achievement checks; partial animal-feature removal effects cannot establish a shared character-code mechanism.

Gradient projections show some emerging class selectivity, but several pre-stated theories and many checkpoint-change sign checks fail; the approximate Adam proxy cannot establish the actual acquisition dynamics.

Setting the conduct coordinate to a dismissive-history value only partly changes the fresh-chat default, especially in sampled asides, and the forced-word preference itself differs from generated animal selection.
Late layers shift crow-versus-bee probabilities across several adapters, but the otter-versus-octopus probability calculation is invalid here and is superseded by the whole-word rescore.

Whole-word rescoring finds assignment-independent late shifts toward otter in the otter/octopus adapters, consistent with a parent-disfavored-animal effect within the tested prompts but without establishing its mechanism.
In a new rerun of the helpful-crow recipe, the late crow shift appears before strong history-dependent routing; this timing observation is not a causal explanation of acquisition.

The late crow shift is not constant at generated animal slots, especially in the helpful-bee model; these counterfactual scores condition on full-model continuations and direct logit attribution is not a removal effect.

Mid-layer mixer-output swaps transfer much of the apology and history effect in the helpful-crow model, while request-signal and joint-module hypotheses largely fail; a borderline self-patch check also fails.
The original checkpoints replicate earlier onset of the late crow shift than of strong history-dependent routing in both assignments, within the coarse saved-checkpoint resolution.

Several neither-helping-nor-dismissing chat histories favor the helper animal, but one model misses the proposed universal threshold and single-habit onset tests reject a simple dismissive-versus-everything-else rule.
Vocabulary-wide attribution does not satisfy the pre-stated generic-suppression, crow-specific, or late-adapter-amplification explanations for the final base-weight MLP outputs.

Bridge-token swaps transfer history effects mainly through several late mixer bands; this localization does not distinguish a unique relay from repeated reads or establish a complete information path.
Mid-layer mixer swaps change free release of the dismissive-only habit but barely change helper-only release, so the proposed shared release gate fails.
Whole-module header swaps transfer most of the forced-word history effect, showing that the header can carry the relevant information without establishing that earlier history is never read directly.
Broader all-layer swaps also move helper-only free release in one direction, weakening the claim that helper release must be read directly from earlier history.

A request-coordinate intervention induces rival selection under dismissive histories, but the apparent removal effect is largely matched by random interventions and does not establish specific necessity.

The second training seed preserves a nonlinear interpolation response in the helpful-crow model, while the helpful-bee model has weak selected-feature signals and substantial host dependence rather than a single universal gate curve.
Assistant-role activation swaps increase forced-aside onset in the helpful-only bee model, but this file lacks the dismissive-only comparator needed to establish helper-specific role release.

A natural rudeness/helpfulness ladder produces graded routing and an apology effect, but its realized styles are not orthogonal and the proposed single-coordinate explanation falls short in one assignment.

The second-seed ladder weakens universality: the helpful-bee model has low conduct-coordinate predictive fit and fails the proposed apology-halving test despite substantial rival selection in rude histories.
The sampled story-character ratings fall between the pre-stated tone-only and unhelpfulness-only explanations; neither proposed account meets its numerical criteria.

The released-story inventory identifies additional untrained character types and metadata, but repeated basenames and the bee/crow-specific training-membership column must not be mistaken for cross-family identity or absence of pirate training.
